references.text: The account of the men of Sodom who surrounded Lot's house and demanded to bring out his guests to 'know' them sexually. This is a direct parallel to the event in Gibeah, with nearly identical language and situation.
Refers to 'worthless men' (bené-beliyaal) who led the inhabitants into idolatry. The same Hebrew expression is used for the men of Gibeah.
Eli's sons are described as 'sons of Belial' (bené-beliyaal) - the same expression used for the wicked men in Gibeah.
Some 'worthless men' (bené-beliyaal) despised Saul. The same expression is used to describe evil people as in Judges 19:22.
Two 'men of Belial' gave false testimony against Naboth. The same terminology for wicked people as in Judges 19:22.
